parts.note: pow is the sound of a punch, so a hit

explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is a meeting or conference, originally a gathering of Native American peoples.

the vicar goes into the bucket, so his letters sit inside the other word

REV, short for Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win out, the verb sense of triumph.

clue.text: Bird's call for service in New York?

indicators.note: the question mark suggests a New York accent, where the T of the call is softened to a D

parts.note: a diner calls 'Waiter!' to get served

explanation.surface: Asks what call a bird makes when it wants service in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: In an American accent the T between vowels is flapped, so the cry to a waiter comes out like the name of the long-legged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wader is a long-legged shore bird, such as a heron or sandpiper.

clue.text: Light a master of sci-fi briefly recalled that seems familiar

indicators.note: called back, so the whole string of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: UV, ultraviolet light

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a Jedi master from Star Wars

explanation.surface: A sci-fi great is briefly remembered in a light that feels oddly familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master of sci-fi' suggests an author such as Asimov; it is the Star Wars Jedi.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the uncanny feeling that a new experience has happened before.

clue.text: Queen of mystery: queen wearing boot but no cap

indicators.note: the boot is worn around the queen, so her letters sit inside
without its cap, the boot loses its first letter

parts.note: a welly is a wellington, a rubber boot
ER, Elizabeth Regina; this is the second, lower-case queen, not the one in the definition

explanation.surface: A detective-story queen is pictured wearing a boot but no hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellery Queen was both the pen name of two American mystery writers and their detective; a welly is a British rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellery is the first name in Ellery Queen, the celebrated American crime-fiction pseudonym.

wordplay.reading: P is the core of apple

parts.note: the question asks what the lone letter is: it is the central letter of a five-letter fruit

explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of APPLE is P, so P is an apple core.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple core is the central part of the fruit left after eating, here taken as its central letter.

clue.text: Expose fanciful husband of Aunti Ash?

indicators.note: a flight of fancy that only works when the imagined name is spoken and heard

explanation.surface: Exposing the imaginary spouse of a tree called Auntie Ash.
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical family of trees: Auntie Ash's husband is Uncle Oak, and those two words run together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncloak is to remove a covering, so to reveal or expose.

clue.text: Agent right to avoid conflict, believe it or not?

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys and sells for another

indicators.note: the conflict avoids the right, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: friction is conflict or discord

explanation.surface: An agent keeps out of conflict, if you can believe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fact or fiction asks whether something is true or invented, the same challenge as believe it or not.

parts.note: the question asks what the lone letter is: it is the first letter of a word for a nation

explanation.walkthrough: STATE begins with S, so S is the head of STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of state is a country's chief public representative, such as a monarch or president.

indicators.note: the cops go inside the room, so their letters sit within

to cop is to nail, catch or arrest, so cops is nails

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops' looks like a noun, police; it is the verb, catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail's pace is an extremely slow speed, a crawl.

indicators.note: wound as in wound up or twisted, so these letters are wrapped into a new order

parts.note: the letters of on, turned round, read as this word

clue.text: Idiot picks things up — but this one won't

picking up sounds is hearing them

explanation.surface: A fool picks things up, though this one never will.
explanation.walkthrough: Cloth ears is British slang for someone who doesn't listen or hear properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called cloth ears ignores or misses what is said, so does not pick it up.

clue.text: Later today, that man's name covered up by drunk

indicators.note: the drunk wraps round the other letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
his, belonging to that man

explanation.surface: Tonight, a man's name is hushed up by someone drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This night is an old-fashioned way of saying tonight, the evening still to come today.

wordplay.reading: K at the end of a rooster

parts.note: the question asks what the lone letter is: it is the last letter of a word for a rooster

explanation.walkthrough: COCK ends in K, so K is the tail of COCK.

clue.text: Tear into solicitor and get high

to rip is to tear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a British lawyer; it is one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip out is slang for being under the influence of a hallucinogen.

wordplay.reading: T is the opener of tin

parts.note: the question asks what the lone letter is: it starts a word for a can

clue.text: Range of particular faculty so heartbreaking?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a university faculty's breadth of courses is so heartbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits one word: its first five letters are the fodder and its remainder, breaking, is the anagram signal. 'Faculty' suggests a university department; it is hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound can be heard, the reach of hearing.

clue.text: Plan a female, perhaps, read out

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: female is an example of a gender, so this is a gender

explanation.surface: A plan for a woman is read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a programme or plan.

wordplay.reading: G is the middle of night

parts.note: the question asks what the lone letter is: it is the central letter of a word for the dark hours

explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of NIGHT is G, so G is mid-NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, the middle of the night.

clue.text: Arid region: I've found it right in middle of South Africa

parts.note: aha is a cry of discovery

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a dry region right in the middle of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sahara is in North Africa, not South Africa, which is the surface's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the vast desert across northern Africa, the archetypal dry region.

wordplay.reading: O at the centre of a rock

parts.note: the question asks what the lone letter is: it is the central letter of a word for a rock

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

clue.text: … two more, ten in group and the others cut
